body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. A drive-by shooting in southeast Bakersfield left one person badly hurt before dawn, and it capped a night of gunfire and weapons calls across the city. Today looks mild and calm — a high near 74 under clear skies, no weather alerts, and air quality sitting in the moderate range. Here's what happened while you slept.

## The Kern Overnight

The most serious call came at 3:55 a.m., when a drive-by shooting in the 500 block of East Belle Terrace in southeast Bakersfield left one person with major injuries. The suspect vehicle, described as a black four-door, was last seen heading northbound on South Real Road toward Stockdale Highway. Earlier, at 1:05 a.m., officers and fire crews were sent to Martin Avenue for a shooting where one person was reported hit. Crews were held back while officers worked the scene, and an air ambulance was asked to stand by.

Gunfire calls came in from several corners of the city. A caller near 10th Street and Lincoln Street counted about six shots over five minutes at 8:28 p.m., and officers went to the 7500 block of a residential street at 12:41 a.m. on a report of multiple gunshots — though a unit already in the area reported hearing none. At 4:30 a.m., a fight at Flower Street and Alta Vista Drive in east Bakersfield grew until a caller reported roughly 30 people there with firearms and bats.

Weapons calls ran the length of the night. A woman asked deputies to a parking lot at 7:31 p.m., saying her boyfriend had battered her and was armed. A man on a scooter with a handgun was reported at a Family Dollar on Highway 58 at 8:20 p.m., and four juveniles with firearms were reported walking northbound on Airport Drive at Washington Avenue at 9:31 p.m. Deputies also went to a home on Southland Court at 12:16 a.m. for a man reported to have a large kitchen knife, and officers followed a lifted SUV on Gosford Road at 12:41 a.m. after a report of a possibly armed man before a subject ran on foot.

The night's worst crash was a head-on collision on Highway 46 east of Curt Road at 1:50 a.m. that hurt three people. One person was trapped in a vehicle and tagged red, a second was tagged yellow, and a third was also treated. Mercy Air was launched and the highway was shut down for a landing zone, but fog turned the helicopter back to base, and both lanes were left blocked. A second head-on crash, north of Sycamore Road at 11:38 p.m., left two cars off the roadway.

## Today's weather

It's 55 degrees right now at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 74 this afternoon and a low around 53 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and there are no active fires to report. Air quality is 56, which lands in the moderate range — fine for most folks, though anyone sensitive to particulates may want to keep an eye on it if you're planning a long stretch outdoors. In short: a good Saturday to be outside, with a light layer for the morning and the evening.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that residents of Pond, the small community near Delano, are pouring concrete and bracing for heavy rain three years after floodwaters wrecked their homes — and they say no help has come from local, county or state government.** Store owner Bilqees Ubadi is building up the ground around her business to keep water out, recalling that she was displaced from her home for about a year after the 2023 flood. Longtime resident Carmen Del Rio told the station she stayed with her son in Wasco for more than a month while they drained and cleaned their house, and that her landlord still hasn't repaired the damage. Residents said they asked officials for help preparing this time and were told Poso Creek, whose contaminated water overflowed into Pond, is unincorporated. Volunteers, some from out of state, did much of the rebuilding last time.

**According to 23ABC, enrollment in Cal State Bakersfield's College of Business and Public Administration has climbed nearly 25% over the past three years, and college leaders say that growth was deliberate.** Dean Dr. Deborah Cours said faculty have expanded outreach to local high schools, community colleges, chambers of commerce and professional groups like the Kern County Society for Human Resource Management, while sharpening programs around industries tied to the local economy — entrepreneurship, accounting, health care management, public administration and a growing supply chain and logistics track. The university has also built relationships with employers including Target Distribution Center, Valley Strong, PepsiCo, Frito-Lay, Grimmway and Bolthouse Fresh Foods, aimed at giving students real-world experience in fields they may eventually enter. The agricultural business program has grown since it launched a decade ago, and the MBA and Master of Public Administration programs continue to draw well.

**KGET 17 tells us a new Angel Walk is bringing hope to domestic violence survivors in Bakersfield.** The walk offers survivors and their supporters a chance to come together, and it adds another visible reminder around town that help and community are within reach. We'll have more on it as details develop.

**23ABC reports that a Sacramento judge has ruled against Nightingale College in its fight with the California Board of Registered Nursing, leaving hundreds of the online school's graduates still waiting to learn whether they can work in California.** Judge Stephen Acquisto denied the college's request for a preliminary injunction, finding in a 12-page ruling that Nightingale was unlikely to succeed on its claims and agreeing with the board's reading of state law — that out-of-state nursing graduates must meet the same minimum clinical training requirements as California graduates. The college had argued the board's 500-hour direct patient care requirement doesn't apply to it and that the state can't regulate out-of-state schools. The board's attorney said hundreds of applicants are affected and warned of potential harm to the public if graduates were licensed without clinical hours in areas like obstetrics and pediatrics.

**KGET 17 also reports that Bakersfield police are searching for a suspect in an east Bakersfield burglary, and Bakersfield Now says the department is asking for the public's help identifying a suspect in a burglary at the Noriega House.** Both cases are open, and investigators are asking anyone with information to come forward. And for football fans, KGET 17 has Week 10 of the high school season covered around Bakersfield and Kern County.

## Something good

The new bike trail along the Friant-Kern Canal is nearing completion, and when it opens it will connect northwest Bakersfield to the Kern River trail. That's a real addition for anyone who rides, runs or just likes a long walk without traffic — a continuous recreational route linking two sides of the community. Worth watching for a ribbon-cutting soon.

## Coming up this week

The Fox Theater has a full slate over the next few days. Tonight, Saturday, October 24, brings two shows: Fred Armisen's "Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome" and BLADE RAVE, both at the Fox. Sunday, October 25, it's REZA | Edge of Illusion, an evening of magic and illusion on the Fox stage. Then Monday and Tuesday, October 26 and 27, J & J Investigations leads Ghost Tours at the theater — a fitting way to close out October. Looking further ahead, the Fox's Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026-2027 is on sale for next year's series.

No public meetings are on the calendar for the coming week as of this morning. If that changes, we'll flag it here. Otherwise, enjoy the mild weather, keep an eye out for your neighbors, and we'll see you back here tomorrow.

top.title: Pond residents brace for heavy rainfall and possible flooding, say no government help has come
